arxiv-2112-12600.title: Gradients of chemical abundances in the Milky Way from H ii regions: distances derived from Gaia EDR3 parallaxes and temperature inhomogeneities 2021 Gradients of chemical abundances in the Milky Way from H ii regions: distances derived from Gaia EDR3 parallaxes and temperature inhomogeneities – A6
arxiv-2112-12600.creator: J. E. Méndez-Delgado, A. Amayo, K. Z. Arellano-Córdova, C. Esteban J. García-Rojas, L. Carigi, G. Delgado-Inglada
arxiv-2112-12600.description: Abstract We present a reassessment of the radial abundance gradients of He, C, N, O, Ne, S, Cl, and Ar in the Milky Way using the deep optical spectra of 42 H ii regions presented in Arellano-Córdova et al. (2020, 2021) and Méndez-Delgado et al.

arxiv-2207-05335.title: An algebraic characterization of self-generating chemical reaction networks using semigroup models
arxiv-2207-05335.creator: Dimitri Loutchko
arxiv-2207-05335.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dimitri Loutchko. The ability of a chemical reaction network to generate itself by catalyzed reactions from constantly present environmental food sources is considered a fundamental property in origin-of-life research. Based on Kaufmann’s autocatalytic sets, Hordijk and Steel have constructed the versatile formalism of catalytic reaction systems (CRS) to model and to analyze such self-generating networks, which they named reflexively autocatalytic and food generated (RAF).

arxiv-2301-06584.title: A joint model of the individual mean and within-subject variability of a longitudinal outcome with a competing risks time-to-event outcome
arxiv-2301-06584.creator: Shanpeng Li, Daniel S. Nuyujukian, Robyn L. McClelland, Peter D. Reaven, Jin Zhou, Hua Zhou, Gang Li
arxiv-2301-06584.description: Abstract Motivated by recent findings that within-subject (WS) visit-to-visit variabilities of longitudinal biomarkers can be strong risk factors for health outcomes, this paper introduces and examines a new joint model of a longitudinal biomarker with heterogeneous WS variability and competing risks time-to-event outcome.

arxiv-2308-12283.title: Constraining Circumgalactic Turbulence with QSO Absorption-line Measurements FLASH ( Fryxell et al. 2000 ; v4.5), matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ; 3.2.2), yt ( Turk et al. 2011 ) , numpy ( Harris et al. 2020 ; v1.22.0), pandas ( Reback et al. 2021 ; 1.3.5)
arxiv-2308-12283.creator: Brad Koplitz, Edward Buie II, Evan Scannapieco
arxiv-2308-12283.description: Abstract Our knowledge of the circumgalactic medium (CGM) is mostly based on quasar absorption-line measurements. These have uncovered a multiphase medium that is likely highly turbulent, but constraints of this turbulence are limited to measurements of the non-thermal width of absorption-line components ( b turb b_{\mathrm{turb}} ) and the line-of-sight velocity dispersion between components ( σ LOS \sigma_{\mathrm{LOS}} ).

arxiv-2311-18706.title: Certified algorithms for equilibrium states of local quantum Hamiltonians
arxiv-2311-18706.creator: Hamza Fawzi, Omar Fawzi, Samuel O. Scalet
arxiv-2311-18706.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hamza Fawzi, Omar Fawzi, Samuel O. Scalet. Predicting observables in equilibrium states is a central yet notoriously hard question in quantum many-body systems. In the physically relevant thermodynamic limit, certain mathematical formulations of this task have even been shown to result in undecidable problems. Using a finite-size scaling of algorithms devised for finite systems often fails due to the lack of certified convergence bounds for this limit.

arxiv-2403-11905.title: NAACL ’25 Tur[k]ingBench : A Challenge Benchmark for Web Agents
arxiv-2403-11905.creator: Kevin Xu Yeganeh Kordi Tanay Nayak Adi Asija Yizhong Wang Kate Sanders Adam Byerly Jingyu Zhang Benjamin Van Durme Daniel Khashabi Johns Hopkins University Brown University University of Washington
arxiv-2403-11905.description: Abstract Can advanced multi-modal models effectively tackle complex web-based tasks? Such tasks are often found on crowdsourcing platforms, where crowdworkers engage in challenging micro-tasks within web-based environments. Building on this idea, we present TurkingBench , a benchmark consisting of tasks presented as web pages with textual instructions and multi-modal contexts.

arxiv-2511-12715.title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
arxiv-2511-12715.creator: Sushrut Thorat, Adrien Doerig, Alexander Kroner, Carmen Amme, Tim C. Kietzmann, ∗ Corresponding authors. Emails: sthorat@uos.de, tkietzma@uos.de
arxiv-2511-12715.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sushrut Thorat, Adrien Doerig, Alexander Kroner, Carmen Amme, Tim C. Kietzmann, ∗ Corresponding authors. Emails: sthorat@uos.de, tkietzma@uos.de. Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present, but also their spatial and semantic relations.

britannica-1911-inn-river.title: Inn (river) (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-inn-river.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-inn-river.description: Article 'Inn (river)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 14), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. It rises at an elevation of 7800 ft., in a small lake under the Piz Longhino, in the Swiss canton of the Grisons. After flowing for a distance of 55 m., through the Engadine it leaves Swiss territory at Martinsbruck and enters Austria. It next plunges through the deep ravine of Finstermünz, and, continuing in the main a north-easterly direction, receives at Landeck the Rosanna.

pmc-10674512.title: Improved Methods for Fourier-Based Microwave Imaging
pmc-10674512.creator: Yuri Alvarez López, Fernando Las-Heras Andrés, Piotr Samczynski, Elisa Giusti
pmc-10674512.description: Fourier-based imaging has been widely adopted for microwave imaging thanks to its efficiency in terms of computational complexity without compromising image resolution. Together with other backpropagation imaging algorithms like delay-and-sum (DAS), they are based on a far-field approach to the electromagnetic expression relating to fields and sources.

pmc-10710412.title: Lysosomes, caspase-mediated apoptosis, and cytoplasmic activation of P21, but not cell senescence, participate in a redundant fashion in embryonic morphogenetic cell death
pmc-10710412.creator: Cristina Duarte-Olivenza, Goretti Moran, Juan M Hurle, Carlos I Lorda-Diez, Juan A Montero
pmc-10710412.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Micromass cultures of embryonic limb skeletal progenitors replicate the tissue remodelling processes observed during digit morphogenesis. Here, we have employed micromass cultures in an in vitro assay to study the nature of cell degeneration events associated with skeletogenesis.

pmc-11336772.title: Process parameters optimization of EDM for hybrid aluminum MMC using hybrid optimization technique
pmc-11336772.creator: Velusamy Mohankumar, Soorya Prakash Kumarasamy, Sivasubramanian Palanisamy, Ajith Kuriakose Mani, Thresh Kumar Durairaj, Mika Sillanpää, Saleh A Al-Farraj
pmc-11336772.description: This study explores how machining parameters affect Surface Roughness (SR), Tool Wear Rate (TWR), and Material Removal Rate (MRR) during Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM) of a hybrid aluminum metal matrix composite (AMMC). The composite includes 6 % Silicon carbide (SiC) and 6 % Boron carbide (B4C) in an Aluminum 7075 (Al7075) matrix.

pmc-11749051.title: Evaluation of the Changes in the Alveolar Bone and Root Length after Maxillary Anterior Tooth Retraction and the Factors Influencing Them
pmc-11749051.creator: S. Harinarayanan, Sanju Somaiah, B. Goutham, Sunil Muddaiah
pmc-11749051.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction:There is a scarcity of studies in which both alveolar bone remodeling and root resorption are simultaneously assessed and compared against possible influencing factors such as rate of retraction and change in inclination.

pmc-12568459.title: Investigation of the effect of debridement combined with antibiotic-loaded bone cement on pain and psychological status in diabetic foot ulcer patients
pmc-12568459.creator: Ke Yang, Yijun Huang, Yinxu Zhang, Yin Wen, Linjie Yan, Wei Chen, Zairong Wei, Kaiyu Nie
pmc-12568459.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the changes in pain levels and psychological status in patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) after accepting the debridement combined with antibiotic-loaded bone cement (ALBC), which offers insight into a comprehensive treatment including pain management and psychological intervention with DFUs.

pmc-12577158.title: Integration of tear fluid biomarkers and machine learning for the early detection of keratoconus
pmc-12577158.creator: Yijun Lin, Yao Yao, Xiaocui Miao, Shumin Tang, Libin Huang
pmc-12577158.description: BackgroundKeratoconus (KC) is a progressive corneal disorder that leads to visual impairment owing to corneal thinning and deformation. While current diagnostic methods are effective in the later stages, early detection of KC remains challenging. This study aimed to investigate the potential of tear fluid biomarkers combined with machine learning (ML) models for the early diagnosis of KC.

pmc-13343763.title: Khat-induced intravesical coiling of a self-inserted urethral serum set: a rare cause of acute urinary retention requiring open bladder surgery
pmc-13343763.creator: Abdullahi Ahmed Ahmed, Khalid Ali Mohamed, Mowlid Mohamud Hassan, Ismail Gedi Ibrahim
pmc-13343763.description: BackgroundForeign bodies within the lower urinary tract are uncommon but clinically significant causes of acute urinary retention and urological emergencies. Self-insertion into the urethra is among the most frequently reported mechanisms and is often associated with psychiatric disorders, intoxication, autoerotic behavior, or altered mental status.

pmc-13398756.title: YIPFα1A expression is regulated by multilayered molecular mechanisms
pmc-13398756.creator: Tokio Takaji, Yurika Nakanishi, Nobuhiro Nakamura
pmc-13398756.description: Yip domain family (YIPF) proteins are five‐pass transmembrane proteins that localize primarily to the Golgi apparatus. These proteins assemble into higher‐order complexes with each α‐subunit pairing specifically with a β‐subunit to form a dimer which then assemble into complexes with two to four dimers.

pmc-13563662.title: Day-to-day associations between social interaction valence and awareness of age-related change
pmc-13563662.creator: Christina Ristl, Lukas Kraiger, Selma Korlat, Sarah E Martiny, Jana Nikitin
pmc-13563662.description: ObjectivesAwareness of age-related change (AARC) reflects how individuals perceive aging through daily gains and losses. Social interactions constitute a central context of everyday life in which such perceptions may be shaped, yet little is known about their short-term interplay in daily life.

pmc-13677037.title: Trimethylamine N-Oxide, a Bariatric Surgery-Associated Host-Microbial Cometabolite, Reduces Colonic Tumorigenesis in a Sex-Dependent Manner
pmc-13677037.creator: Yang Bi, Maria Glymenaki, Maria A Valdivia-Garcia, Mu Wang, Kai Yee Eng, Edward Lin, Nana Gletsu-Miller, Julian R Marchesi, Ron Smits, Mona El-Bahrawy, Nadia Guerra, Jia V Li
pmc-13677037.description: Background & AimsTrimethylamine N-oxide is a host–microbial cometabolite that significantly increases following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Although trimethylamine N-oxide is associated with cardiovascular diseases, its role in colorectal cancer remains unclear.MethodsFabplCre;Apc15lox/+ mice, a genetically altered colorectal cancer model, together with murine macrophages and human colonic cancer cells (HCT-116), were used to investigate the impact of trimethylamine N-oxide on colonic tumorigenesis.

uslaw-usc-t31-s712.title: 31 U.S.C. § 712 — Investigating the use of public money
uslaw-usc-t31-s712.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t31-s712.description: United States Code, Title 31 (Money And Finance); Chapter 7 (Government Accountability Office); Subchapter II (General Duties And Powers). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Comptroller General shall— (1) investigate all matters related to the receipt, disbursement, and use of public money; (2) estimate the cost to the United States Government of complying with each restriction on expenditures of a specific appropriation.

uslaw-usc-t7-s2252.title: 7 U.S.C. § 2252 — Reimbursement of Production and Marketing Administration appropriations for costs of procuring agricultural commodities for nongovernmental agencies or foreign governments
uslaw-usc-t7-s2252.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s2252.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 55 (Department Of Agriculture). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Applicable appropriations available to the Production and Marketing Administration current at the time services are rendered or payment therefore is received may be reimbursed by nongovernmental agencies or foreign governments (by advance credits or reimbursements) for the actual or estimated costs, as determined by the Production.
